title: Where to Watch the Dune Movies Before Part Three
excerpt: Both Dune films stream on HBO Max, with rental options everywhere else. Full watch order, runtimes and what to rewatch before Part Three.
author: StarScoop Daily Staff
imageAlt: Dune Part Two backdrop — where to watch the Dune movies before Part Three
metaDescription: Where to watch Dune and Dune: Part Two before Part Three — HBO Max, rental platforms, watch order and what to rewatch. Updated guide.
content:
With Dune: Part Three coming, the obvious question is where to catch up. Short answer: both films stream on HBO Max, and both are available to rent almost everywhere else.

Here's the full breakdown, watch order, and an honest answer on what you actually need to rewatch.

Where to Stream Dune (2021)

Denis Villeneuve's first film covers roughly the first half of Frank Herbert's novel — House Atreides arriving on Arrakis, the betrayal, and Paul and Jessica's escape into the desert.

Subscription: HBO Max (also via the HBO Max Amazon Channel), YouTube TV

Rent or buy: Amazon Video, Apple TV, Google Play Movies, YouTube, Fandango At Home, Plex

⭐ IMDb: 8.0 · Director: Denis Villeneuve · Released: 2021

Where to Stream Dune: Part Two (2024)

The second film covers Paul's integration with the Fremen, his relationship with Chani, and his transformation into something the first film spent two hours warning you about.

Subscription: HBO Max (and HBO Max Amazon Channel), YouTube TV, Spectrum On Demand

Rent or buy: Amazon Video, Apple TV, Google Play Movies, YouTube, Fandango At Home, Plex

⭐ IMDb: 8.4 · Cast: Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya, Rebecca Ferguson, Javier Bardem, Josh Brolin, Austin Butler, Florence Pugh

Availability note: the platforms above reflect US listings. Streaming rights differ by country and rotate over time — in India, the UK and Australia the films have appeared on different services. Check your local listing before planning an evening around it.

The Watch Order

Straightforward, because there are only two:

  1. Dune (2021)
  2. Dune: Part Two (2024)

They are one continuous story split in half. Part Two opens essentially where Part One ends and assumes you remember everything.

What about the older adaptations? David Lynch's 1984 Dune and the 2000 Sci-Fi Channel miniseries both exist and both have their defenders. Neither is required — Villeneuve's films are a separate adaptation of the same novel, not a continuation. Watch them out of curiosity, not obligation.

Do You Need to Rewatch Both?

Honestly, no — and this is where most catch-up guides pad things out.

If you've seen both recently: you're fine. Skip to the last 30 minutes of Part Two, which is where the setup for Part Three actually lives.

If you've seen both but it's been a while: rewatch Part Two only. It recaps enough of the first film's events through dialogue, and it contains everything Part Three builds on — Paul taking the throne, Chani walking away, the Fremen legions going to war.

If you've never seen either: watch both, in order, ideally close together. Roughly 5 hours 20 minutes total. It genuinely works better as one long film than as two separate viewings.

What to Pay Attention to Before Part Three

If you're rewatching with Part Three in mind, three things matter more than the spectacle:

  • Paul's visions. He sees the holy war coming and spends two films trying to avoid it. Part Three is about failing.
  • Chani's skepticism. She is the only major character who never accepts the messiah framing. Her final scene in Part Two is the emotional thread going forward.
  • The Bene Gesserit. Their manipulation of prophecy is deliberate and long-running. Understanding that changes how you read Paul's rise entirely.

Get those three and you'll follow Part Three without any homework.

Where to Watch It in Cinemas

When Part Three arrives, see it on the largest screen you can. Villeneuve shoots for large-format presentation and both previous films lost meaningful visual information on small screens.
